newsitem.title: USA: U.S. rail freight traffic up from year ago -- AAR.
newsitem.headline: U.S. rail freight traffic up from year ago -- AAR.

text.p: U.S. rail freight traffic in the week ended February 15, fueled by increases in grain and automotive, rose from the same week in 1996, the Association of American Railroads said Thursday.

AAR reported 344,107 carloads in the February 15 week, up 1.4 percent from 339,492 a year ago. In that total, it said grain carloads totaled 27,063, up 10.1 percent from 24,591 a year ago, and loadings of motor vehicles and equipment stood at 22,212, an eight percent rise from 20,574 last year.
AAR said intermodal volume in the February 15 week, which does not include carloads, totaled 165,954 trailers and containers, a 5.9 percent increase from 156,696 last year.
Ton-mile volume also rose 1.9 percent to 27.1 billion from 26.6 billion a year ago. The ton-mile, a measure of freight transportation, equals one ton of freight hauled one mile.

AAR also reported increases in carloads of petroleum, which climbed 8.2 percent to 5,808 in the week from 5,370 in the year-ago week. Grain mill products also rose 9.1 percent to 10,640 carloads from 9,752, while lumber and wood products increased 6.1 percent to 5,250 carloads from 4,950.

But primary forest products loadings declined 11.7 percent to 7,028 from 7,955 last year, while nonmetallic minerals fell 2.7 percent to 8,371 carloads from 8,600. Metals and related products also fell 3.8 percent to 12,111 carloads from 12,591.
In the first seven weeks of 1997, AAR said carloads rose 5.3 percent from the same period last year. Intermodal traffic rose 4.9 percent, while ton-miles climbed 6.2 percent.

AAR also said traffic rose on Canada's two transcontinental railroads in the latest week compared to the same week in 1996. It said new trailers and containers totaled 25,205, up 19.4 percent from last year, while new carloadings stood at 55,035, a 2.7 percent rise from a year ago.
